strengths: Novel problem formulation of self-contradiction in MLLMs with clear motivation and intuitive framing
Compelling empirical analysis showing 85%+ of misalignments stem from weak generation, validated via external oracle
Learning dynamics theory (Proposition 1) extending prior work to multimodal setting with aligned training trajectories
Important negative finding: Nonunified score cannot distinguish co-degradation from co-improvement, highlighting metric limitations
Comprehensive analysis within scope including both in-distribution and out-of-distribution evaluation
Practical self-improvement methods without explicit external rewards, with consistent improvements across metrics
Well-presented paper with clear takeaways and informative visualizations
weaknesses: Severely limited model evaluation: only Janus-Pro tested despite claiming insights about MLLMs broadly; Show-O, Chameleon, Emu3 evaluation mentioned as future work but essential for main claims
Fundamental contradiction: method depends on Qwen2.5-VL-72B oracle to construct training data and validate improvements, undermining the 'self-improvement without external signals' narrative
Theoretical analysis restricted to single-token settings with linear networks; gap between simplified theory and actual model behavior is substantial; multi-token extension only future work

Metric reliability issues: WinRate metric is circular (compares against Qwen oracle by design); UniDet sufficiency not justified; core finding that Nonunified score fails to distinguish co-improvement/degradation undermines its utility

Co-degradation analysis superficial: only tested with extreme corruption (fixed token ID); practical noise patterns not explored; proposed solution requires external validation, again contradicting self-improvement claims
Limited comparison with concurrent methods: Hermesflow, UniRL, Got-R1 mentioned but not systematically compared; T2I-R1 comparison limited by protocol choice
Modest empirical improvements: 5-10% in most metrics, consistent but not dramatic; unclear if practically significant
Incomplete analysis: vague explanation of 7B vs 1B differences using 'model priors'; limited guidance on method applicability; no ablation studies on hyperparameters (learning rate 1e-7, 120 epochs)
Missing critical analyses: no human evaluation, no error analysis, limited computational cost discussion, no analysis of prompt type dependencies
Curriculum learning component is incremental: simple difficulty ordering with modest improvements (5-15%) over standard methods; no comparison with alternative curriculum strategies

strengths: Identifies an important practical problem: non-unification in MLLMs with comprehensive empirical validation across 6 diverse architectures and multiple benchmarks, controlled for task difficulty confounders

Proposes a simple yet effective self-improvement framework without external signals that achieves up to 20% generation and 16% unification improvements, surpassing external-reward baselines (T2I-R1, HermesFlow)
Novel non-unification metric that measures internal consistency rather than relying on external evaluators, avoiding external bias

Sophisticated theoretical contribution: extends learning dynamics theory to multimodal setting with formal analysis (Propositions 1-2) explaining co-improvement via shared eNTK, supported by comprehensive empirical evidence (Figures 7, 13-16)
Empirically discovers and documents co-improvement effect in post-training (80% from false positive correction), an underexplored phenomenon
Rigorous empirical methodology with human evaluation validation, careful stratification by difficulty, and clear attribution to weak generation vs. misunderstanding
Excellent reproducibility: detailed algorithms, hyperparameter tables, complete results across benchmarks, and clear implementation details
weaknesses: Severely limited model coverage for self-improvement: only 2 models tested (Janus-Pro-7B and Show-o, both relatively small), with generalization to other architectures and larger models unverified; acknowledged but critical limitation

Theoretical analysis relies on questionable assumptions: uniform prompt prior (Eq. 7) is unrealistic, shared-tokenizer assumption doesn't match all architectures, first-order Taylor approximations may be loose, and eNTK sharing claims lack rigorous proof

Metric reliability concerns: Qwen-based evaluation shows 19.67% discrepancy on hard tasks undermining confidence in 'Weak Generation' classification for complex reasoning; non-unification score circularly depends on understanding quality
Conceptual novelty of method is limited: self-improvement reduces to using internal understanding as reward signal—not fundamentally different from external reward models except for the signal source
Circular reasoning in validation: improvements correlate with internal gap (ρ=0.53, Figure 4), meaning method works better where problem is worse, somewhat tautological
Small post-training datasets limit scalability: Janus-Pro 1,326 samples, Show-o 226; even with curriculum learning ~1,091 additions—tiny compared to pre-training scales and many samples remain unused
Statistical rigor issues: no error bars, confidence intervals, or multiple runs; single-run results without seeds; small sample sizes for some benchmarks (Science-T2I: 49 chemistry examples)
Incomplete baseline comparisons: T2I-R1 only on Janus-Pro, HermesFlow only on Show-o; head-to-head comparisons on same models with same data lacking
Curriculum learning component feels ancillary: modest gains in Table 1 (C-SFT vs SFT), epoch 10 choice appears empirically driven without principled justification (Section F.2)

Limited scope: text-to-image only, English prompts only, understanding evaluation limited to alignment scoring; generalization to other modalities/reasoning tasks unclear; computational costs underspecified
